realFindings.title: The P0 stableKey/definedTermRefs fix shipped with no backfill - real, currently-live ContractRule rows in this shared Postgres instance still exhibit the exact pre-fix defect, silently, right now
realFindings.discoveryMethod: Read-only inspection of the already-committed real companies fixture-fwrg-2021-credit-agreement-co (53 real ContractRule rows, 95 total across both real companies with non-empty definedTermRefs) and fixture-lsb-2023-abl-credit-agreement-co, persisted before this session's fix (createdAt 2026-08-26, before the 2026-08-30 fix).
realFindings.evidence: getRuleSourceTrace(REAL_FWRG_CO, <a real rule with non-empty definedTermRefs>).definedTerms is currently EMPTY, even though rule.definedTermRefs.length > 0 and a matching real DefinedTermNode.termName genuinely exists (confirmed by an explicit raw-name lookup) - i.e. the rows still store the pre-fix raw term-name strings, not stableKeys. Reproduces identically for the real LSB company. validateDefinedTermTargetsExist(REAL_FWRG_CO) currently reports 117 real, live validation issues.
realFindings.whyThisIsAnIndependentFindingNotAMereRes: docs/phase-3f1-5-r-residual-foundation/13-source-trace-audit.json certified the FIX ITSELF (the persistContractRules code path, verified going forward - which this certification's own fresh-ingest sample above independently re-confirms is correct). It did not audit whether the fix reached ALREADY-PERSISTED real data in the shared certification database. This certification found, by direct real-Postgres inspection, that it did not: the fix is real and correctly shaped, but is not retroactive, and nothing re-triggers affected documents' recompilation automatically.
realFindings.whyThisIsSilentAndMaterial: getRuleSourceTrace's definedTerms returning an empty array is indistinguishable from the correct, legitimate state 'this rule has no term dependencies' - there is no error, flag, or discrepancy surfaced anywhere in the API. A future 'Why?' UI or Ask Headroom feature consuming this trace today, for these 95 real, already-compiled covenant rules across two real regression packages, would silently omit every defined-term dependency with no indication anything is wrong - the exact 'material source-trace corruption' / silent-material-failure shape Architecture Invariant #37 exists to make structurally impossible. The known, disclosed stage-promotion.ts filter bug (docs/foundation-remediation/13-remaining-foundation-risks.json) means the real validation issues this defect DOES correctly generate (117 of them, confirmed above) never actually block anything in practice - so there is no live safety net catching this.
realFindings.notADowngrade: This is not downgraded because a fix (a one-time backfill script recomputing stableKeys for already-persisted definedTermRefs, or a forced recompile of the two affected real packages) would be straightforward - per the certification charter, ease of fix is not grounds for downgrading a BLOCKER.
realFindings.remediationSuggested: A backfill migration/script that re-derives each existing ContractRule.definedTermRefs entry's correct document-scoped stableKey using the exact same formula persistContractRules now uses (or a forced re-run of the real compiler for any already-ingested document), plus fixing the disclosed stage-promotion.ts message-format filter so validateDefinedTermTargetsExist's real findings actually gate promotion. Not implemented in this certification (production code is frozen for this phase; this is a data/backfill concern, not a code-logic concern the fix itself needs).

realFindings.title: resolveUniquePersistedNodeByRef never normalizes a 'Section '/'Article ' citation prefix before matching against the structural index's own bare section-number format
realFindings.discoveryMethod: Root-cause isolation of why sourceNodeId is null for every one of the 130 real ContractRule rows currently in this shared Postgres instance (a fact discovered while investigating S11-F1) - not previously named in any prior phase's own audit.
realFindings.evidence: A direct, isolated real-Postgres test: persisting a document with a real SECTION node '6.01' and calling the real, unmodified resolveUniquePersistedNodeByRef(nodeIndex, documentId, '6.01') correctly resolves; calling the SAME function with 'Section 6.01' (the EXACT literal format already found live in fixture-fwrg-2021-credit-agreement-co's own real ContractRule.sourceSectionRef column) returns undefined, even though the target section genuinely, uniquely exists. persistContractRules (lib/contract-model/compiler/persistence.ts) passes rule.sourceSectionRef into this function completely unnormalized.
realFindings.impactAssessment: Unlike S11-F1, this is an honest OMISSION (sourceNode: null) rather than a misleadingly-empty-looking-complete list - the section-reference STRING itself (rule.sourceSectionRef, e.g. 'Section 6.01') remains visible on the ContractRule row and in getRuleSourceTrace's own rule.sourceSectionRef field, so a consumer is not misled into believing no section reference exists at all; they simply do not get a deep link to the exact physical DocumentNode span, and lose the char-span/heading-level cross-check this certification otherwise confirms works correctly for citations that happen to already be bare-formatted.
realFindings.scopeConfirmation: All 130 real ContractRule rows currently in this shared Postgres instance have sourceNodeId=null - this citation-prefix mismatch is a plausible, independently-confirmed contributing mechanism, though a separate, also-independently-confirmed factor (a stale, pre-current-parser STRUCTURE-stage cache specific to these two fixture companies' own committed compiler-run history, producing only 1 coarse ARTICLE-level DocumentNode instead of 418 real fine-grained nodes) is also a sufficient explanation for these SPECIFIC two companies' rows and was not disentangled from this citation-format defect within this certification's scope.
realFindings.remediationSuggested: Normalize both sides of the match (strip a leading 'Section '/'Article ' token, matching whatever normalization the real RULES-stage prompt's own citation format requires) inside resolveUniquePersistedNodeByRef or immediately before calling it in persistContractRules. Not implemented in this certification (production code frozen).

definedTermRefsStableKeyFixReverificatio.requirement: Construct or find a real rule that references a defined term, and confirm getRuleSourceTrace's definedTerms field is now correctly populated (non-empty) where before the fix it would have silently returned empty.
definedTermRefsStableKeyFixReverificatio.freshIngestResult: CONFIRMED - all 8 freshly-ingested real-text samples above show non-empty, correctly-matched definedTerms.
definedTermRefsStableKeyFixReverificatio.preExistingDataResult: CONFIRMED THE FIX DOES NOT RETROACTIVELY APPLY - see S11-F1. The fix is genuinely correct for the code path; it does not repair data persisted before it shipped.

verdictRationale: The getRuleSourceTrace/persistContractRules stableKey fix itself is independently re-confirmed correct via 8/8 real, freshly-ingested samples matched against actual real source text. However, this certification independently discovered that the fix, as shipped, left real, currently-live, already-compiled ContractRule data (95 rules across two real regression packages) silently exhibiting the exact pre-fix defect right now, in the same shared Postgres instance this certification (and any real customer environment that compiled documents before 2026-08-30) uses - a live, reproducible, silent material source-trace gap matching the BLOCKER definition's own 'material source-trace corruption' example. This is a BLOCKER on the FOUNDATION (the fix's completeness across the system's actual persisted state), not a retraction of the code-level fix's own correctness, which is independently confirmed sound.
